newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 (𝐌𝐀𝐔𝐋𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐈𝐍𝐂𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐍𝐓)

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || At approximately 1732H on September 25, 2026, Titay Municipal Fire Station Shift A personnel responded to a reported mauling incident at Barangay Kitabog, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay.

Upon arrival at the scene at approximately 1738H, the responding team ensured scene safety before attending to the patient, identified as a 40-year-old male. The patient was found seated on a chair, conscious, alert, and oriented, with a patent airway and spontaneous respirations. Initial assessment revealed lacerations to the left parietal area and the left ulnar aspect of the forearm. An odor consistent with alcohol was also noted on the patient's breath.

Immediate first aid was provided by applying direct pressure to the wounds using sterile gauze to control bleeding. The lacerations were cleansed with an appropriate irrigating solution and dressed with sterile gauze. Vital signs were assessed and recorded at BP 120/80 mmHg, PR 88 bpm, RR 20 cpm, SpO₂ 98%, and temperature 36.3°C. The patient was continuously monitored for any changes in condition.

The patient was subsequently transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for further medical evaluation and management.

Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient was properly endorsed to the physician on duty for continuity of care. The responding personnel and BFP Ambulance later safely returned to quarters.

On September 22, 2024, Titay Municipal Fire Station trained teachers and students of San Antonio National High School as members of the School Emergency Response Team (SERT), equipping them with essential knowledge and practical skills in emergency preparedness, first aid, basic firefighting, and rescue. BFP Titay Conducts Fire Square Roadshow for Titay District Student Leaders

TITAY, Zamboanga Sibugay — September 12, 2026 — More than just classroom lessons, fire safety education came alive as the Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) conducted a Fire Square Roadshow for student leaders of the Titay District at Titay National High School, Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The activity equipped young leaders with essential knowledge and practical skills in fire prevention, basic firefighting, rescue, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH), empowering them to become active advocates of safety and preparedness in their schools, homes, and communities.

The activity aimed to strengthen the knowledge, skills, and preparedness of student leaders in preventing and responding to fire and other emergencies. It provided participants with practical lessons and demonstrations on basic firefighting, rescue techniques, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH).

Adding an interactive approach to fire safety education, BFP Titay also facilitated online fire safety games, allowing participants to test and reinforce their knowledge through engaging and interactive activities.

The Fire Square Roadshow emphasized the important role of students as fire safety advocates and responsible members of the community. By equipping young leaders with essential fire safety knowledge and emergency response skills, the BFP seeks to help build a culture of preparedness and strengthen community resilience.
